name: Globe Civil Projects Ltd
title: Globe Civil Projects Ltd - 544424 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: EPC civil contractor reports Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin ~17% and PAT up 40%, but receivables and inventory rose faster than revenue and management guides only 10-15% growth on a ~INR700 crore order book.

summary.headline: Globe Civil Q1 FY27 revenue (total income) rose 37.26% YoY to INR929.23 million; PAT up 40.42% to INR7.09 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated total income for Q1 FY27 was INR929.23 million versus INR676.98 million a year earlier, up 37.26% YoY. EBITDA rose 33.03% to INR15.80 crore with a stated margin of 17.01%, and PAT rose 40.42% to INR7.09 crore (net margin 7.63%). Management attributed growth to projects won after the IPO (Central University Bathinda, Haryana Cricket Association stadium, Kanpur) and said working capital was elevated by pre-final/final bills and early material procurement. Management guided to 10-15% growth in FY27 on the existing order book, with order book targeted to reach INR1,200-1,500 crore.

segments.name: Institutional / education
segments.commentary: Management called education its main focus, citing IITs, IITs/IIMs/NITs as major revenue sources; recent bids include Central University Tamil Nadu and IIM Visakhapatnam. IIT Delhi and an INR100 crore IIT order were mentioned.

segments.name: Sports infrastructure
segments.commentary: Two small sports projects of about INR50 crore each done, and a ~INR200 crore stadium (Jhajjar) under execution, with management aiming to build eligibility for bigger sports projects. Stadium revenue to date was about INR30-35 crore, and completion is targeted in about 15 months.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 10-15% from the existing order book, excluding any new project wins.
Expected FY27 execution of about INR300-350 crore from the ~INR700 crore order book, with the largest revenue in the last quarter.
EBITDA margin expected to be maintained at around 17% (similar margins), and management said margins are sustainable for the next one to two years.
Target to add at least INR500 crore of new orders within 3-12 months, taking the order book to about INR1,200-1,300 crore; next milestone INR1,500 crore by year-end.
Management says it wants order book at least 3x annual turnover.
capex_capacity: Management said it can handle 10-15 projects simultaneously; 11-12 projects are currently running.
Single-project eligibility is INR500-650 crore in normal projects; larger projects possible via joint ventures.
Existing setup could support revenue of INR500-600 crore without a major increase in fixed cost.
Inventory rose about INR162 crore, partly from early procurement of material (e.g., tiles) in Feb-Mar 2026 ahead of price rises for the Bathinda project.
Mobilisation advance (up to ~10% of contract value against bank guarantee) available but not availed on Bathinda or the recent IIT project.
demand_pricing: About four to five tenders (~INR800 crore) were pending opening; bids placed at two to three per month, including Bihar, Tamil Nadu, Visakhapatnam and Nagpur.
Selective bidding favoured central government and funded projects; competition cited as 5-6 bidders versus 10-15 on NHAI tenders.
Management described competition as healthy with decent margins, not heavy under-bidding.
Top 5 projects contribute about 70% of turnover; one private client (DPS) and one cricket stadium are the main private projects, the rest are government.
Repeat clients include CPWD (about 20 years), NBCC (fifth or sixth project) and DPS (three projects in total).

qa_highlights.question: What drove Q1 revenue growth and what share of revenue came from which projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Post-IPO wins (Central University Bathinda, Haryana Cricket Association, Kanpur) drove growth; Bathinda structure work and NBCC project contributed most. A new project typically takes 6-8 months to reach full revenue flow.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the order book and what pipeline exists?
qa_highlights.answer: Current order book about INR700 crore; four tenders (~INR800 crore) awaiting opening; target at least INR500 crore new orders in 3-12 months, taking book to INR1,200-1,300 crore; next milestone INR1,500 crore by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables and inventory rise, and what is being done on cash conversion?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables rose on Q4 final and pre-final bills (Aligarh NBCC billing expected to close by 15 September; Telecommunications India Limited by 30 September). Inventory rose on material bought in Feb-Mar 2026 ahead of price increases. Routine government and DPS bills take 30-40 days to realise.

qa_highlights.question: Why were some projects delayed and what is the stadium contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Stadium start was delayed by statutory approvals; it started scaling from March. Stadium revenue to date is about INR30-35 crore. Management said approvals for government projects now sit within EPC scope, making them faster.

qa_highlights.question: Will the current margins be sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is confident the current margins (about 17% EBITDA) are sustainable for the next one to two years.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR700 crore order book will be executed in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects INR300-350 crore of execution in FY27, based on current monthly run-rate of INR30-40 crore.

risks_watch: Receivable days elevated: final bills pending on NBCC Aligarh and Telecommunications India Limited; collection timing is key to cash flow.
Inventory and working capital rose faster than revenue; watch whether it normalises as orders scale.
Order inflow needed to reach INR1,200-1,500 crore target; four tenders (~INR800 crore) pending with no guaranteed wins.
Project start delays from statutory approvals (Bathinda, cricket stadium) can push revenue recognition out by 6-8 months.
Heavy reliance on government clients and top 5 projects (~70% of turnover).
summary.management_tone: Confident on execution and margins, but guidance is conditional on new order wins. Management was candid about delays, receivable timing and the number of pending tenders. Several answers were vague or repetitive on order targets and FY27 growth.
key_quotes: We always believe that we should have at least 3 the turnover -- 3x order book of the turnover.
Yes. We're confident that this margin are sustainable for the next couple of years.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue growth of 10-15% (midpoint 12.5%) on the existing ~INR700 crore order book, with expected execution of INR300-350 crore and a target of at least INR500 crore of new orders within 3-12 months; backing is order-book driven but no new capacity is being added and the existing setup can support INR500-600 crore revenue.
